title: Accounting finance manager
overviewOfRole: Manage and implement accounting and finance systems and processes to support effective decision-making and organisational strategy.

knowledges.detail: The regulatory framework of financial accounting that applies to sole traders, partnerships, companies, charities, and public sector organisations.
Accounting concepts and standards in UK GAAP and IFRS, as applicable to sole traders, partnerships, companies, charities, and public sector organisations.
The technology available for financial accounting, reporting, and internal controls, for example, iXBRL.
Approaches to analysing issues relating to competitors, stakeholders, and market trends, for example, ratio analysis, trend analysis, stakeholder analysis, and competitor analysis.
Approaches to data analytics using technology to visualise findings from the analysis of financial and non-financial data from internal and external sources.
The requirements of the Information Commissioner under GDPR, and other stakeholders.
Digital technology and protocols used to protect data from cyber-attacks and data corruption.
The principles of legal, professional, and ethical frameworks, including regulations regarding money laundering, criminal finance, data protection, health and safety, computer misuse, and cybercrime.
The principles of digital systems management to ensure compliance with all relevant legal, professional, and ethical frameworks.
The principles and significance of reconciling internal system records with external information sources, such as banks and suppliers.
The purpose and techniques of budgeting and forecasting required to manage revenue, expenditure, and cash flow.
The use of digital technology to compile, manage, and report on budgets.
Approaches to creating cash flow forecasts.
The use of digital technology to forecast, monitor, and report on movements in an organisation’s cash flows.
Approaches used to analyse the financial and non-financial impacts of management decisions.
The use of digital technology to provide management reports that assist decision-making.
The importance of taxation in society and its impact on government policy.
The relationship between UK taxation and the accounting and finance function within organisations.
The taxation reporting implications and obligations arising from organisational or client decision-making.
Principles of digital technology used to process data and fulfil organisational and HMRC digital taxation reporting requirements.
The importance of the internal and external audit functions and the significance of providing audit teams with the information they require to fulfil their duties.
Strategic planning techniques used by organisations to analyse, develop, and implement strategy.
Approaches to using digital technology to analyse, communicate, monitor, and report on strategy implementation and the achievement of strategic objectives.
Approaches to identifying and evaluating quantitative and qualitative factors that influence business performance.
The use of technology to collect, analyse, and communicate quantitative and qualitative data.
The sources of finance available to organisations.
Approaches to using technology to identify and apply for finance and maintain credit relationships.
The legal and organisational framework for managing receivables, credit control, and internal and external relationships.
Approaches to using technology to manage credit control for internal and external stakeholders.

The principles and practice of designing, implementing, and maintaining internal controls that mitigate risk and prevent issues such as errors relating to quality, accuracy, fraud, cyber-attacks, and other irregularities.
Approaches to internal controls for both manual and digital systems and processes, taking into consideration the control environment.
Approaches to managing external relationships that affect the organisation.
Approaches to using digital technology to produce relevant information for stakeholder reports, such as Integrated Reporting or Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) reports.
Principles of effective staff recruitment, training, appraisal, mentoring, and management.
Approaches to using digital technologies to appraise, monitor, and manage staff.

behaviours.detail: Demonstrates conscientious and diligent attention to detail that strives for completeness and accuracy.
Adopts a rigorous and empirical approach to analysing data and research, investigating facts and gathering expert opinion before recommending action.

Commits to continuing professional development (CPD) by keeping up to date with legislation, releases from standard setters, advances in digital technology and its application to accounting and finance, and guidance from HMRC.

Works objectively and effectively, both independently and as part of a team, adopting a reflective approach and seeking continuous improvement in internal and external relationships, including reviewing their own performance and that of their team.
Acts with professional scepticism, maintaining a questioning mind, remaining alert to conditions that may indicate possible misstatements due to error or fraud, and critically assessing evidence.

Exercises professional judgement and upholds professional values, applying ethical standards to make informed decisions about courses of action that are appropriate to their organisation or client, including acting in the public interest.

Creative, innovative, and enterprising when seeking solutions to business needs; responds positively and adaptably to feedback and the need for change; and remains open to new ways of working and emerging management theories.

skills.detail: Prepare financial statements, or extracts thereof, in accordance with International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) and UK Generally Accepted Accounting Practice (GAAP).
Identify and use appropriate digital technology to achieve desired outputs in the context of producing statutory or financial reports.
Analyse financial and non-financial internal data and compare it with benchmark data, such as that from competitors, stakeholders, and market trends.
Use data analytics tools, visualise findings, make evidence-based recommendations for future action, and communicate them.
Interpret and implement the latest guidance on secure data management to satisfy the requirements of the Information Commissioner and GDPR.
Implement protocols and technology that minimise risks to data integrity and cybersecurity.
Evaluate internal and external factors relevant to the organisation's operational compliance with all necessary legal, professional, and ethical frameworks.
Apply the principles of digital systems management to ensure continued compliance with all relevant frameworks applicable to the organisation.
Analyse and interpret the reasons for differences between internal and external source documentation and produce reconciliations that clearly identify those differences and the required actions.
Create budgets and forecasts using the most appropriate tools and techniques.
Interpret budget reports to evaluate the reliability of forecasts and identify variances that require further action.
Calculate and interpret cash flow forecasts.
Interpret cash flow reports and identify future actions required to manage cash balances.
Apply management accounting techniques to assist decision-making within the organisation.
Interpret management reports and utilise a variety of media, including verbal communication, to deliver advice that influences management decisions.
Interpret and apply HMRC rules and guidance to produce tax calculations and statutory returns.
Implement and manage systems and processes that gather the information required by HMRC.
Analyse and summarise organisational or client decision-making and its impact on taxation reporting and obligations.
Implement and manage technology to satisfy HMRC reporting requirements for digital taxation.
Produce information required by internal and external auditors in a clear format.
Evaluate strategic options, taking into consideration the impact of internal and external factors.

Develop, communicate, and deliver operational plans that meet strategic objectives, including setting targets and key performance indicators (KPIs), managing resources, and monitoring and measuring outcomes to establish operations effectively, efficiently, and economically.

Interpret quantitative and qualitative data to assess business performance and utilise a variety of media, including verbal communication that demonstrates emotional intelligence, to make recommendations.
Analyse and interpret the process of how data is collected, extracted, analysed, and reported.
Evaluate the impact of different sources of finance on an organisation, including associated risks, and recommend appropriate finance options.
Advise organisations on and implement technology to raise finance and maintain credit relationships.
Design and manage a compliant credit control system that meets strategic objectives relating to customers, insurers, and cash flow.
Implement technology that enables the delivery of a credit control system that meets strategic objectives.
Analyse, design, implement, communicate, monitor, and review internal control systems and processes that mitigate risk, including the risks of error, fraud, and cyber-attacks.
Document organisational manual and digital internal controls, identify weaknesses, and make practical recommendations for improvement.
Develop and maintain effective relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
Identify relevant information to be included in stakeholder reports.
Identify potential improvements to HR policies and activities, such as recruitment, training, appraisal, mentoring, and management.
Evaluate the effectiveness of digital technology used to appraise, monitor, and manage staff.

duties.dutyDetail: Manage financial accounting, monitoring, and reporting systems, procedures, and internal controls in line with changes in technology, including automation, artificial intelligence, cloud-based applications, and Making Tax Digital (MTD).
Analyse financial and non-financial data on competitors, stakeholders, and market trends, and make recommendations for future action.
Manage accounting and financial systems for cyber security and data integrity.

Ensure that all operations and systems comply with relevant legislation, regulations, and codes of governance and professional ethics, while demonstrating an understanding of the duties and responsibilities of an accounting finance manager.
Conduct periodic accounting and finance reconciliations, reviews, and evaluations to ensure records are accurate and resources are used efficiently, effectively, and economically.
Manage the budgetary process, analyse variances, research and explain change, and make recommendations accordingly.
Proactively monitor, interpret, and control cash flows, spot trends, and forecast requirements.

Collate and produce accurate financial and management accounting reports to specified deadlines, and support internal managers and or external clients in understanding financial information to facilitate decision-making
Oversee and manage the production of tax computations and returns for HMRC in line with Making Tax Digital (MTD), and advise internal managers and external clients on their obligations.
Liaise with internal and external auditors to ensure that annual monitoring and reporting requirements are met.

Contribute to the implementation of organisational strategy, business plans, and business planning by using accounting, finance, and system-wide applications to provide robust evidence for effective decision-making.
Analyse and interpret a wide range of financial information for internal and external stakeholders.

Research, analyse, and report on factors influencing business performance, making recommendations to improve outcomes, for example by reducing costs, improving profitability, enhancing quality and customer satisfaction, increasing efficiency and productivity, and supporting sustainability.
Research and identify sources of finance, demonstrate an awareness of risk, assist in arranging new sources of finance, and maintain existing lines of credit and credit relationships.
Manage the credit control function by maintaining receivables (sales ledger), monitoring cash flow, managing customer relationships, and ensuring compliance with the relevant legal framework.
Develop and maintain internal controls that monitor and manage financial risk to safeguard the organisation's assets and mitigate liabilities.

Understand the importance of external relationships to the organisation and be able to maintain them. External relationships may include clients, customers, suppliers, auditors, solicitors, bankers, and statutory organisations such as HMRC, Companies House and the Financial Conduct Authority.
Recruit, train, appraise, mentor, and be responsible for the day-to-day management of their accounting and finance team.
